title: Replace Question Marks in String to Minimize Its Value
summary: Given a string s with lowercase English letters and '?' characters, replace each '?' with a lowercase English letter to minimize the string's value.
statement: Given a string s with lowercase English letters and '?' characters, replace each '?' with a lowercase English letter to minimize the string's value. The value is the sum of cost(i) for all indices i, where cost(i) counts the number of characters equal to s[i] that appeared before i. Return the lexicographically smallest string with the minimum value.
constraints: s contains lowercase letters and question marks.
A completed string costs the number of equal-character pairs, equivalently the sum of equal predecessors at every index.
Minimize that cost, then return the lexicographically smallest minimizing completed string.
hints: Adding one occurrence of a letter increases pair cost by its current frequency.
Repeatedly choose the least frequent letter, breaking ties alphabetically; sort all chosen letters before filling question-mark positions.
Use a heap of (frequency,letter), increment the chosen frequency, then place the sorted chosen multiset left to right.
Minimum marginal-cost choices minimize total pairs; rearranging the chosen multiset does not change cost, and sorted placement minimizes the final string.
editorial: Minimum marginal-cost choices minimize total pairs; rearranging the chosen multiset does not change cost, and sorted placement minimizes the final string.

tests.explanation: Using three distinct smallest letters gives minimum cost zero and lexicographically smallest result abc.
The missing letters b and c avoid increasing the two existing a characters, producing abac.
